name: Kenya
summary: The Mara migration, Amboseli elephants under Kilimanjaro, the Rift Valley lakes, the Swahili coast and a capital with a national park on its doorstep.
window_alt: A zebra on a red earth track with a snow-capped peak far behind
when: The migration crosses the Mara July to October; January to March is calving.

entries.caption: Where the Safari Was Invented
entries.description: The Maasai Mara at first light, and everything the word safari has meant for a century.
entries.subject: acacia and open grassland in the Maasai Mara at sunrise

entries.caption: The Great Rift Valley
entries.description: The escarpment drops away below the Naivasha road, holding a chain of soda lakes and dormant volcanoes.
entries.subject: the Great Rift Valley escarpment and floor seen from the Naivasha road

entries.caption: Wildlife on the Savannah
entries.description: The Big Five, plus the reticulated giraffe and Grevy's zebra that live nowhere south of here.
entries.subject: elephants crossing the plain at Amboseli beneath Kilimanjaro

entries.caption: The Great Migration
entries.description: Between July and October a million wildebeest cross the Mara river, and the crocodiles are already waiting.
entries.subject: wildebeest crossing the Mara river during the great migration

entries.caption: Mount Kenya, 5,199 m
entries.description: Equatorial glaciers, giant lobelia, and a trekking route to Point Lenana that needs no technical climbing.
entries.subject: the jagged glaciated peaks of Mount Kenya above the moorland

entries.caption: Thomson's Falls
entries.description: The Ewaso Ng'iro drops seventy-four metres into a fern gorge at Nyahururu, on the way north to Samburu.
entries.subject: Thomson's Falls dropping into the fern gorge at Nyahururu

entries.caption: Flamingo Country
entries.description: Nakuru, Bogoria and Elementaita hold soda water, hot springs and flamingo in numbers that change by the season.
entries.subject: flamingos massed on the shallows of Lake Nakuru

entries.caption: The Swahili Coast
entries.description: Diani, Watamu and Lamu: white sand, warm Indian Ocean, and a coastline that traded with Arabia for a thousand years.
entries.subject: white sand and dhows on Diani Beach on the Indian Ocean

entries.caption: Kakamega, the Last of It
entries.description: The only Kenyan remnant of the Guineo-Congolian rainforest that once ran clear across the continent.
entries.subject: dense canopy and hanging vines inside Kakamega Forest

entries.caption: Balloon Over the Mara
entries.description: Up before dawn, an hour over the plains at treetop height, and breakfast on the grass where you land.
entries.subject: a hot-air balloon over the Maasai Mara plains at sunrise

entries.caption: Maasai and Swahili
entries.description: Two Kenyas: the cattle-keeping highlands and the coral-stone, Arabic-inflected coast.
entries.subject: Maasai elders in red shuka cloth on the open plains

entries.caption: Samburu and Maasai
entries.description: Samburu in the northern drylands, Maasai in the south, both still moving cattle between seasonal grazing.
entries.subject: a Samburu warrior with beaded ornaments in the northern drylands

entries.caption: Nyama Choma and Ugali
entries.description: Goat roasted over charcoal, maize meal, sukuma wiki, and coastal biryani that came in by dhow.
entries.subject: nyama choma roasting over charcoal at a Nairobi grill

entries.caption: Lamu Cultural Festival
entries.description: Dhow races, donkey races, henna and taarab music in the alleys of a town with almost no cars.
entries.subject: dhow racing during the Lamu cultural festival

entries.caption: Beadwork and Kisii Stone
entries.description: Maasai beadwork, Kisii soapstone carving, and kiondo sisal baskets made the way they always were.
entries.subject: Maasai women stringing beadwork ornaments

entries.caption: Fort Jesus, Mombasa
entries.description: Portuguese, built 1593, taken and retaken nine times — now UNESCO World Heritage above the old harbour.
entries.subject: the coral ramparts of Fort Jesus above Mombasa old harbour

entries.caption: Lamu Old Town
entries.description: The oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement, carved doors, coral rag walls and no room for a car.
entries.subject: carved wooden doors and coral stone alleys in Lamu Old Town

entries.caption: Nairobi, Green City in the Sun
entries.description: The only capital on earth with a national park inside the city limits, and lions in sight of the skyline.
entries.subject: the Nairobi skyline seen across Nairobi National Park

entries.caption: Coral Stone and Carved Doors
entries.description: Swahili coral-rag houses with inner courtyards, and doors carved in Lamu and shipped up the coast.
entries.subject: an ornately carved Swahili door in a coral stone wall in Lamu

entries.caption: Matatus and Markets
entries.description: Painted, over-amplified matatus, Maasai Market on rotation through the week, and tea at every stop.
entries.subject: brightly painted matatu minibuses in a Nairobi street

entries.caption: The Conservancies
entries.description: Community conservancies lease grazing land back for wildlife, and the lease pays the schools around the Mara.
entries.subject: a community conservancy ranger team on patrol near the Maasai Mara

entries.caption: Walking Hell's Gate
entries.description: The one Kenyan park you can walk and cycle through, with gorge scrambling and geothermal steam.
entries.subject: cyclists on the track between the cliffs of Hell's Gate National Park

entries.caption: Camps on the Mara
entries.description: Small tented camps on private conservancies, night drives and off-road access the main reserve does not allow.
entries.subject: a luxury tented safari camp overlooking the Maasai Mara plains

entries.caption: Rhino, Counted Daily
entries.description: Ol Pejeta and Lewa run some of Africa's most closely monitored rhino populations, funded by the beds on the property.
entries.subject: black rhino grazing on the Ol Pejeta conservancy at dawn

entries.caption: Kilimanjaro from Amboseli
entries.description: The mountain is in Tanzania; the view of it is in Kenya, and it is only clear for an hour at each end of the day.
entries.subject: elephants beneath Mount Kilimanjaro seen from Amboseli at sunrise

entries.caption: Chalbi and Marsabit
entries.description: The desert north: Chalbi's salt pan, Marsabit's forested crater and the road down to Lake Turkana.
entries.subject: the salt pan and dunes of the Chalbi desert in northern Kenya

entries.caption: Magical Kenya
entries.description: Migration, glacier, reef and desert inside one border, with the infrastructure to see all four in a fortnight.
entries.subject: acacia silhouetted against a red sunset on the Kenyan savannah
